requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
**Verdict: the tests have a gap.** The `habeas coverage-check` exit status, which is the "returning success only when…" obligation, is never asserted.

**What the subject requires.** `requirements.test-coverage.check` says `habeas coverage-check` must:
- check saved coverage against the threshold and function requirements;
- return success only when every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence;
- not build, not execute tests, not collect coverage, and not invoke an assessment model.

The threshold, function, and exception obligations belong to the cited requirements and their own tests. I did not reassess them.

**What the tests cover.**
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` runs the standalone `habeas coverage-check` against saved data. It uses a `cargo` shim that records any non-`metadata` invocation, and a sentinel file written by a captured test.
  - It asserts that the shim's "forbidden" marker was not created, so there was no build or collection.
  - It asserts that the sentinel was not recreated, so no test ran.
  - It asserts that the retained files are byte-identical afterwards.
  - This adequately covers the "MUST NOT build / execute tests / collect coverage" clauses, at least for `cargo`-driven work.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` covers a pass and a failure through the combined `habeas test` flow.
  - The pass shows "Coverage check passed".
  - The failure comes from a zero-execution nested `fn[hidden]` and gives a non-zero exit.
  - It also asserts that the enclosing `fn[outer]` is not reported as unexecuted.

**Gap: the `coverage-check` exit status is never asserted.**
- The CLI mapping lives in `src/main.rs#enum[Command]` and the `CoverageCheck` arm of `fn[main]`. That arm runs `execution_coverage::check` and exits with `i32::from(!report.passed)`.
- The full-flow test runs `habeas test`, not `coverage-check`. That is a different arm, `Command::Test`, which calls `execution_coverage::test`.
- The standalone test runs `coverage-check` but only asserts that stdout contains "File execution coverage". It does not assert the exit status or whether the outcome was a pass or a fail. Its saved data is a partial run filtered with `-E test(second)`, so the expected outcome is not established.
- I searched `tests` for `coverage-check`. The only other hit is `tests/setup.rs`, which checks guidance text.
- A plausible violation the tests would accept: `habeas coverage-check` exits 0 even when the report has failures, or the exit code is inverted. This breaks "returning success only when every applicable obligation is satisfied or excepted". The unit tests in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs` exercise `check_in` and `report.passed`, not the CLI exit.
- The mapping is a conditional transformation, `i32::from(!passed)`, so it does not qualify for the pass-through exemption.

**Smaller gap: no test for "MUST NOT invoke an assessment model".**
- No reviewed test sets up a detector for model invocation. The shim in `fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` only intercepts `cargo`.
- I found no model invocation in `src/execution_coverage`. The only match for "model" is a comment in the check tests: `fn[reviews]` in `check.rs` says production evidence is authored by a model.
- I treat this as secondary. The first gap is the decisive one.

A test that runs `habeas coverage-check` on a passing fixture and a failing fixture, and asserts exit codes 0 and non-zero respectively, would close the main gap.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
